entries.title: Proverbs 23:1
segments:
With a ruler; who has invited thee to a sumptuous entertainment. 
 
When tempted to the immoderate indulgence of appetite, we should lay a severe restraint upon ourselves; for it impairs the faculties of soul and body, stupefies the conscience, and degrades us in our own estimation and that of our fellow men.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:2
segments: Put a knife to thy throat; to prevent excess in eating; a figurative way of saying, Restrain thine appetite at all costs.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:3
segments: Deceitful meat; they promise much pleasure, but end in pain and shame.  The reference is to the immoderate indulgence of appetite at the tables of the great, which not only injures the guest, but degrades him in the eyes of all present.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:4
segments: Thine own wisdom; the wisdom which makes riches the chief good, and thinks by prudent management to get and keep them.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:5
segments: The consideration of the uncertainty of all earthly possessions, leads every wise and considerate man to provide for himself "a treasure in the heavens that faileth not."

entries.title: Proverbs 23:6
segments:
That hath an evil eye; the grudging man, or the crafty and malicious man, who invites the unwary to his table only to deceive and ensnare them. 
 
It is a common device of crafty dissemblers to flatter and bestow favors only that they may ensnare and plunder.  Against the hospitality of such men the young should guard as against thieves and burglars.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:8
segments:
Vomit up; that is, it will end in bitterness. 
 
  Sweet words; addressed by him to thee.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:9
segments: The man who treats with contempt the counsels of the wise, releases them from the obligation of further admonition, and makes his own ruin certain.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:11
segments: Their redeemer; God, who defends the cause of the poor and fatherless.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:13
segments:
Shall not die; shall be reclaimed from sin, and so saved from death. 
 
Our heavenly Father prefers that we should weep now under his chastising rod, rather than perish at last through want of timely discipline.  Herein every wise parent will imitate God's example in his dealings with his children.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:18
segments: An end; that is, in the present connection, a prosperous end; or, a reward, namely, to those that fear God.  Compare

entries.title: Proverbs 23:29
segments: The imbecility and loathsome disease which the habit of using intoxicating drinks produces, and the dreadful power of this habit to perpetuate itself; the poverty, contention, and wretchedness with which it fills the family circle; the quarrels, murders, debaucheries, and crimes that follow in its train, are well understood at the present day.  Whoever allows himself in this debasing habit, or furnishes to others the intoxicating cup, is without excuse.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:31
segments: Moveth itself aright; goes down smoothly.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:34
segments: Lieth down; to sleep on the deck of a ship, or at the mast's head; representing the disordered condition of the drunkard in soul and body, which causes him to reel, and makes all around and within him a troubled and heaving sea.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:35
segments:
Was not sick; was not pained from the blows, because of my insensibility. 
 
  It; the intoxicating cup.
